about.title: About me
paragraphs: I'm an industrial engineer and a teacher. Before I started programming, I spent about fifteen years in industry: power distribution, manufacturing, maintenance, logistics and production. That's where I learned how much it takes for information to be recorded correctly and on time.

As an administrator at Tecnoclima, I implemented the plant's equipment database and saw the problems with its management system firsthand. When I learned to code, I built the one that 160 people across 11 plants use today.
Today I work as a frontend developer on an education platform, where my two backgrounds come together: the technical one and the teaching one.

why.title: Why me
why.text: I had worked for 5 years as general administrator at one of the plants, so I knew firsthand what needed to be recorded. I started the system as a personal project and, once I showed it, the company decided to adopt it.

details.title: The problem
details.text: The company tracked its activity with Access forms on a network of three computers. Technicians filled in paper sheets that the tool-room supervisor then typed in; data took 3 days on average to be entered, and sometimes up to 2 weeks. The system had been designed by someone outside the business, and data entry was often a source of problems.

details.title: What I built
details.text: The data model, the API and every view; I also manage the deployment on a virtual machine. Role-based web access (supervisors plan and create work orders, technicians see their assignments and log progress, administrators monitor activity, managers review history and trends); work-order entry designed to require as little typing as possible; full history per unit; Excel import and export.

details.title: The outcome
details.text: Technicians log their own work and the information is available the same day. Management uses the history and the trend in service requests to back budget decisions.

items.context: Education platform with an AI tutor · ~20,000 users · expanding through partnerships with schools
highlights: Adapted a desktop-first platform for mobile after metrics showed that most users accessed it from their phones.
Built the main screens from the designs: landing, home, content, settings, lessons, groups and reports.
Developed the hooks that extended the migration from Redux to React Query across the whole platform.
Review the visual and pedagogical quality of AI-generated teaching tools.

details.title: Mobile adaptation
details.text: The platform had been designed for desktop, but metrics showed that most users came from their phones. I adapted the interface and improved transitions for touch devices.

details.title: Main screens
details.text: When a designer joined the team, I implemented each screen with its components (sidebar, lesson navigation and assessments, group cards) and worked with the designer to adjust whatever wasn't technically feasible.

details.title: React Query
details.text: Building on the Tech Lead's initial implementation, I developed the custom hooks to roll it out to the rest of the platform. The result: fewer server requests, a more consistent cache, and hooks that respond better when several components use them in the same view.

details.title: AI-generated tools
details.text: I check that instructions are easy to understand, numbers are legible, colors aren't confusing, and nothing overlaps or overflows.

highlights: Implemented component variants for A/B tests on an e-commerce product page.
Introduced git hooks to check formatting and linting before every push, which made code reviews simpler.

details.title: A/B tests
details.text: Component variants triggered by URL flags or traffic source, built with Preact and DOM manipulation and integrated into an existing page.

details.title: Git hooks
details.text: The project didn't enforce any formatting, so a small change came mixed with hundreds of reformatted lines. I proposed and implemented hooks with Prettier and ESLint; diffs started showing only what had actually changed, and the team adopted them.

highlights: Built components and their Storybook documentation for an app whose views are generated dynamically from a JSON configuration (components, tables and filters).

items.context: Software startup · International team, working in English
highlights: Built the <link>Kelp Digital</link> and Anagolay websites end to end from designs.
Kept a Lighthouse standard of 95+ (reaching 96–98) by optimizing images, loading and SEO.
Ensured compatibility across Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari while working in an international, English-speaking team.

details.text: I built complete pages in SvelteKit (structure, navigation, Tailwind configuration), plus SEO, Twitter Cards and image optimization, until they cleared the Lighthouse threshold of 95 the company required. I also contributed with SvelteKit to Macula, the product's application.

highlights: Created and maintained automated tests for the Citi (Mexico) mobile app on Android and iOS, after training in test automation with Java and JUnit.
Assessed full stack projects by students in online courses, giving constructive feedback on their code and progress.

items.summary: Mathematics, Physics, Marketing and technical workshops.

Maintained a georeferenced database, did functional testing of the internal work-order system, built pivot-table reports and trained technical offices.
